content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the organisation of the nervous system
Explain the roles of the central and peripheral nervous systems
Distinguish between sensory, relay, and motor neurones
Describe the pathway of information through the nervous system

allows the body to detect and respond to changes in the environment. It uses electrical impulses to carry information rapidly, enabling quick responses to stimuli. The nervous system works alongside the endocrine system to coordinate body activities.
The nervous system is divided into:
Connects CNS to rest of body
Relays information to and from brain
Autonomic nervous system further divided into:
Carries impulses from receptors to CNS
Carries impulses from CNS to effectors

content.text: Nerves and neurones are the same thing
Neurones are individual cells; nerves are bundles of neurone fibres
Some reflexes are coordinated by the spinal cord alone
Sensory neurones only respond to touch
Different sensory neurones detect different stimuli (light, sound, etc.)
It works closely with the endocrine system
Nerves connecting CNS to rest of body
Neurone carrying impulses from receptor to CNS
Neurone connecting sensory to motor neurones in CNS
Neurone carrying impulses from CNS to effector
Muscle or gland that carries out response
Change in environment that triggers response
Nervous system divided into CNS (brain + spinal cord) and PNS (peripheral nerves)
Three types of neurones: sensory, relay, and motor
Information pathway: stimulus → receptor → sensory → relay → motor → effector → response
Receptors detect stimuli; effectors carry out responses
Voluntary responses involve conscious thought; involuntary are automatic
Nervous system is fast but short-lived; endocrine is slower but longer-lasting
